+Run `python3 development/dependency-audit.py` from any directory to verify the fixed, bounded set of source and evidence inputs. It opens each named path component relative to an anchored checkout directory descriptor with no-follow directory and leaf flags. It rejects symlinks at every path component, missing, non-regular, oversized, malformed, stale, or identity-incomplete inputs, and does not accept input path arguments. If Python or the host lacks the required `dir_fd`/no-follow flags, it refuses with an explicit unsupported-capability result. The API and platform capability contract follows the [Python 3.12 `os.open` documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/os.html#os.open). `development/dependency-audit/report.json` binds every pinned input hash and the exact target/package identity sets; the verifier also checks its fixed SHA-256 so an edited report cannot bless altered inputs. Captured metadata preserves the assigned worktree's absolute paths for provenance; the verifier checks source files against the pinned current checkout bytes and checks graph identities rather than treating those absolute paths as current source.
 
 The exact bounded command invocations, outputs, toolchain identity, and their hashes are retained in `../evidence/dependency-g01/worker/commands/`. Cargo ran through `development/build-fixture.sh cargo` with the assigned shared artifact/cache roots, `--locked`, and `--offline`. One initial `cargo tree` attempt used unsupported `proc-macro` as an edge kind and exited 1; the corrected `--edges all` and normal/build/features commands succeeded. That failed invocation is retained as a negative command outcome. No source manifests, Rust, protobuf, build scripts, or toolchain files were edited. This audit does not claim the full project gates have passed.
 
-The verifier checks the report's fixed SHA-256 before parsing any report fields. Negative metadata/package fixtures use a temporary copy of the verifier pinned to each deliberately mutated fixture report, so they exercise the underlying bounded parsers and identity checks without changing the submitted tool or report.
+The verifier walks the lexical checkout root from `/` using `dir_fd` plus `O_NOFOLLOW`, then opens all fixed relative directories and files through those anchored descriptors.
